source.title: Reverse Replay of Hippocampal Place Cells Is Uniquely Modulated by Changing Reward.

confidence_rationale: Two-edged for MECH-319. On the supporting side: forward and reverse replay are categorically distinguishable and functionally dissociable event-types, which is consistent with replay carrying a discrete tag that a categorical gate could read. On the tension side: reverse replay scales its rate with reward magnitude (more replay at increased reward, less at decreased), i.e. replay of real experience is recruited FOR reward learning -- so MECH-319's write-suppression must be confined to non-realized simulation passes and cannot be a blanket replay block. Strong methods; confidence moderated by the mixed direction.
failure_signatures: Reverse replay rate increases with increased reward and decreases with decreased reward, demonstrating that this replay class is actively used for reward-based learning -- direct tension with any gate that would suppress arbitration-weight updates during replay indiscriminately.

The forward/reverse distinction is correlated with function but the paper does not show a categorical write-admit/block signal; the binary admit/block character MECH-319 posits is inferred from the dissociation, not measured.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Forward and reverse hippocampal replays diverge in their response to changing reward: only reverse replays increase their rate at increased reward and decrease at decreased reward, while forward replays are unchanged -- demonstrating a functional distinction between replay directions and a unique relationship between reverse replay and reward processing.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-319 posits a CATEGORICAL write-gate keyed to the simulation tag of the caller. Ambrose et al. show that replay events are not a homogeneous stream but come in functionally distinct, separable classes -- evidence that the substrate carries discrete replay categories that differ in their relationship to learning, consistent with a tag the arbitration-layer gate could condition on (admit real-experience reward replay, block ghost/DMN passes).
mapping.mapping_caveat: The categories distinguished here are forward vs reverse REAL-experience replay, not realized vs simulated/ghost passes; MECH-319's specific tag (simulation-mode of the caller) is a different cut than the one measured. And the reward-scaling of reverse replay shows replay IS used for learning, so the mapping must own that the gate cannot be a blanket replay block -- it must be selective to non-realized data.
mapping.source_context: Rats; CA1 ensemble recording during a spatial task with experimentally varied reward, comparing forward vs reverse replay rates at reward locations.

confidence_components.notes: Neuron, Foster lab, rigorous ensemble electrophysiology with a clean reward manipulation. Mapping fidelity moderate: supports the discriminable-replay-class premise but the measured cut differs from MECH-319's simulation tag, and the reward-scaling result is in partial tension with a write-suppression gate. Hence mixed direction.
